From order to unpredictability.

An inspectable, reversible chaos-based dynamic key encryption experiment.

THE LOGISTIC MAP
xn+1 = r xn(1 − xn)

With r = 3.99, small changes to the starting value can lead to very different sequences. Each iteration contributes to a new key byte.

Control parameter
3.99
Initial state (latest run)
—
Warm-up iterations
1,000
Passphrase derivation
PBKDF2 · SHA-256 · 100,000 rounds
Integrity check
HMAC-SHA-256
01

Derive the key

A fresh 16-byte nonce salts PBKDF2. Its 64-byte output is split into a chaos seed and an authentication key.

02

Generate the dynamic stream

The key seeds the logistic map. After 1,000 warm-up iterations, two map steps produce each key byte, mixed with a derived-key byte.

03

Encrypt and authenticate

Each UTF-8 byte is XORed with its key byte and the preceding ciphertext byte. HMAC authenticates the version, nonce, and ciphertext.

c[i] = p[i] ⊕ k[i] ⊕ c[i−1]
04

Verify and reverse

Check the authentication tag, regenerate the same stream, and reverse the XOR operation to recover the exact text.

p[i] = c[i] ⊕ k[i] ⊕ c[i−1]
An educational algorithm. Floating-point chaos has finite precision and is not a substitute for audited cryptography. Entropy and avalanche statistics do not prove security. Use a standard authenticated cipher such as AES-GCM for real secrets.
